anchors.paper_title: A functional overlap between evidence accumulation, confidence, and changes of mind in the pre-supplementary motor area and insula
anchors.reason: The paper title and abstract directly describe the recording and analysis of data from the specific task (perceptual decision making) associated with this dataset.

metadata.methods_description: High-gamma activity (average power modulation in five non-overlapping frequency bands between 70-150 Hz) was recorded from implanted sEEG electrodes using a Micromed recording system at 512 Hz sampling rate. Data were segmented from trial onset (start button click) to trial offset (post-confidence response). Trials and channels with high epilepsy-related artifact were removed. Behavioral data including stimulus onset, response times, and confidence judgments were recorded for each trial.

citation_details.title: Cortical evidence accumulation for perceptual experience occurs irrespective of reports
citation_details.author: François Stockart, Ramla Msheik, Alexis Robin, Lenka Jurkovičová, Dorian Goueytes, Martin Rouy, Radek Mareček, D. Hoffmann, Liad Mudrik, Róbert Román, Milan Brázdil, Lorella Minotti, Philippe Kahane, Michael Pereira, Nathan Faivre
citation_details.abstract: Summary Perceptual experience is a multi-faceted, dynamical process, tackled empirically through measures of stimulus detectability and confidence. To assess if stimulus detection and confidence can be explained by evidence accumulation, a form of sequential sampling of sensory evidence, we analyzed high-gamma activity from stereo-electroencephalographic data of 29 participants partaking in 3 pre-registered experiments. In an immediate-response experiment, individual channels and decoded multivariate latent variables in the visual, inferior frontal, and anterior insular cortices displayed functional markers of evidence accumulation. In two further experiments, this signal in the ventral visual cortex differentiated between (1) seen and unseen stimuli in delayed detection, (2) high and low intensity stimuli during passive viewing, and (3) levels of confidence when stimuli were seen. citation_details.title: Neural basis of concurrent deliberation toward a choice and confidence judgment
citation_details.author: Miguel Vivar-Lazo, Christopher R. Fetsch
citation_details.abstract: Decision confidence plays a key role in flexible behavior and (meta)cognition, but its underlying neural mechanisms remain elusive. To uncover the latent dynamics of confidence formation at the level of single neurons and population activity, we trained nonhuman primates to report choice and confidence with a single eye movement on every trial. Monkey behavior was well fit by a bounded accumulator model instantiating parallel processing of evidence, rejecting a serial model in which the choice is resolved first followed by post-decision accumulation for confidence. Neurons in area LIP reflected concurrent accumulation, showing covariation of choice and confidence signals across the population, and within-trial dynamics consistent with parallel updating at near-zero time lag. citation_details.title: Leaky evidence accumulation accounts for perceptual confidence and subjective duration
citation_details.author: Ramla Msheik, Emma Sirouet, Simon P. Kelly, Nathan Faivre, Michael Pereira
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Perceptual consciousness is defined as the subjective experience associated with the processing of sensory cues from the environment. Subjective experience unfolds over time and is accompanied by a sense of confidence, yet the mechanisms underlying these two properties remain elusive. Here, we propose a computational mechanism that accounts not only for the onset of subjective experience but also its subjective duration and associated feeling of confidence. Our model assumes that a percept becomes conscious when an ongoing, leaky accumulation of sensory evidence surpasses a perceptual threshold and stops being conscious when it falls back below the threshold due to leakage. Crucially, this perceptual threshold can be lower than the decision threshold for reporting the percept. Moreover, our model derives confidence in accurately detecting sensory evidence from the maximum reached by the evidence accumulation process following stimulus onset. citation_details.title: MetaRDK
citation_details.author: Dorian Goueytes, François Stockart, Alexis Robin, Lucien Gyger, Martin Rouy, Dominique Hoffmann, Lorella Minotti, Philippe Kahane, Michael Pereira, Nathan Faivre
citation_details.abstract: MetaRDK is a stereo-electroencephalography (sEEG) dataset from pharmacologically intractable epilepsy patients performing a perceptual decision-making task with metacognitive confidence judgments. Participants discriminated the direction of random dot motion while providing confidence ratings, with neural recordings capturing high-gamma activity (70-150 Hz) throughout task performance. This dataset enables investigation of neural mechanisms underlying evidence accumulation, decision confidence, and changes of mind in human intracranial recordings.
